metadataRoles.notes: Roles that an explicit metadata marker decides: an OData V4 vocabulary term (matched by its lower-case qualified-name suffix, first match wins) or a V2 sap:semantics value (lower case).

temporalVocabulary.notes: Words of a field label or name. created/changed mark administrative timestamps; start/end mark interval bounds for the temporal plan. No other pair of business events is ordered: which one comes first is not known from words. datePairStart/datePairEnd are the narrower interval markers of the start/end date coherence rule, kept separate because widening them would pair more fields. clock words name the time of an event (ReceiptDate, ReceiptTime and ReceiptDateTime are one event).

coherenceVocabulary.notes: Name tokens of the generic coherence rules. Tokens are compared after splitting camel case, underscores and hyphens, in lower case.

vdmFieldGroups.notes: Field-name profiles of SAP S/4HANA interface views. Names are normalized: lower case, without separators. Each profile is applied only when a scenario opts into its coherence rule.

lifecycle.source: SAP S/4HANA equipment interface views: equipment lifecycle flags

processingStatus.source: SAP S/4HANA bank statement interface views: bank statement item posting status

modelOutputFilters.notes: Filters for values the fine-tuned model proposes. Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions compiled with the u flag and tested against the value trimmed, with whitespace collapsed and lower-cased (en-US). In a field template, {fields} stands for the escaped alternation of the field's name, label and description, normalized the same way.

codeTexts.notes: Code/text vocabulary. The text of a code is the field a Common.Text or sap:text annotation names, or a string sibling whose name is the code's name followed by one of textSuffixes (PaymentGroup / PaymentGroupText). A field whose name ends in a text suffix is a name form: it never keeps a role in codeRoles, which yield codes; nameRoleOf gives the role that names such a code, and a code role without one is withdrawn. A code's text comes from a supplied or fixed row, a record name (recordNames: the host's ICU display names of regions, currencies and languages, or the units bank), or the first generated text of the code; nothing is invented for a code none of them names, which keeps what it holds (empty unless a tier wrote a value that is no text). A text holds a run of at least minimumTextLetters letters, and a field shorter than that holds no text. Suffix words are English word forms of OData and ABAP field naming (SAP Fiori design guidelines, text arrangement of codes; ABAP Dictionary data element short, medium and long texts).

realismGuard.notes: When a generated string is withheld for echoing a name of the service (a property, entity or entity set name, label or description, or a trailing run of its words) followed by a number. A name of at least minimumEchoedWords words is an echo wherever it occurs (Unit Price 1); a shorter one only when its column counts it up with at least minimumCountedNumbers different numbers, since one word and a number is often a real value (Room 14). A number after a word the service does not use is never withheld.

realismChecks.notes: Vocabulary and thresholds of the realism checks in src/quality, which read final rows to find values no real data would hold. They are kept apart from the generator's own vocabularies so that a check does not share the generator's blind spots. Form words name the form of a field rather than its subject (OData and ABAP naming: description, text, code, key); text field words, as the last word of a name, make a field hold text, never codes; country words name a country key (land: the ABAP country key LAND1). Time, clock, qualifier and event words find the ordered pairs of a row (created before changed, from before to). A column is of a kind, holds codes or holds cities only when at least the given share of its values do; a pattern is shown only from the given number of rows. A code is at most maximumCodeLength capitals, digits, underscores or hyphens. A multi-word value is at least minimumSharedWords words, and two fields share a list only when they share minimumSharedValues such values. A placeholder echoes a service name of at least minimumEchoedWords words, or a service name its column counts up with minimumCountedNumbers different numbers.

typedFloor.notes: Generation parameters of the typed floor for strings no role fills. A field the metadata makes a code (a text, value list or value help) takes a code shape with an ordinal drawn from codeOrdinals values, so codes repeat across rows like a code list. Every other string abstains, whatever its length: a short column may hold a flag, a word or a code, and nothing in its metadata says which.

temporalSpread.notes: Generation parameters, not facts about any domain. When generation wrote both events of an ordered pair (a temporal-plan constraint) at one instant, the later one moves later: in all rows but one in unchangedOneIn, by an exponentially distributed number of days (the inter-event time of a Poisson process) with mean meanGapDays, capped at maximumGapDays, plus a uniform number of minutes in gapMinutes; a time of day moves by the minutes only, within its day.

generationRanges.notes: Generation parameters, not facts about any domain: the inclusive integer ranges values are drawn from where no metadata bounds them. endDateGapDays: days an end date lies after its start when both come from the date role banks. dateRepairGapDays: days a coherence repair moves an end after its start when a pair came out reversed. streetNumber: the house number before a street name. bankStatementPage: page numbers of a bank statement. count: a count held in a string field, also bounded by the field's length. decimalPlaces and dimensionExponent: the decimal places and the power of ten of a unit dimension. Facets (precision, scale, MaxLength) still apply.

geography.notes: Place fields of a row follow one country. The anchor is the row's country code field (a field planned with anchorRole, or named as a country code); every field planned with a leaf role is drawn from the location record of that country. When an entity has several country fields, a place field follows the one sharing the most name words with it. Roles of another party (contextLeafRoles: a bank and its BIC) follow only a country field whose name shares a context word with theirs (PayeeCountry for PayeeBic); a bank is not assumed to be in the record's own country. Roles follow ISO 3166 (country, region), ITU-T E.164 (telephone numbering), ISO 9362 (BIC) and the IANA time zone database.

rolePolicy.notes: Runtime routing policy, kept apart from the fingerprinted role registry the classifier head pins: changing it never invalidates a packaged head.

organizationNameEvidence.notes: Name-only evidence that a string field displays the name of an organisation, used by the lexical fallback. The word before the last display word of a field name is the head of the name and names what is displayed (English compound nouns are right-headed): the field qualifies when that word is a subject word, or when there is no such word and the name of its entity has a subject word. A field whose head word names another subject, or a word of the entity other than a subject word, does not qualify. Digits are ignored. Subject words are the organisation words of the org_name lexical rule; display words are the OData and ABAP word forms of a display name.

thresholds.notes: Uncalibrated fallbacks. A calibrated classifier head carries its own per-role route thresholds, which take precedence; these apply only to decisions that arrive without one.

route.notes: Minimum classifier confidence to route a field when neither the head nor the role registry gives a threshold.

conflict.notes: Minimum classifier confidence to overrule a disagreeing lexical candidate when the role registry gives no conflict threshold.

lexicalConfidence.notes: Confidence recorded for a role accepted from the lexical fallback.

statistics.notes: Confidence a decision without its own route threshold must reach to count as routed in coverage statistics and tier attribution.
